fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. The queen of Sheba heard about Solomon's fame and came "…to test him with difficult questions." (2 Chronicles 9:1). Solomon was the one with the reputation, and she wanted to see if it held up. I would have brought a pop quiz and a box of cookies, but she brought a whole caravan.

A treaty is a fine guess, but the passage doesn't say that. It says she came "…to test him with difficult questions." (2 Chronicles 9:1). She sat down and "…spoke with him about all that was on her mind." The text gives questions, and a treaty isn't mentioned.

Not quite, baker. The text says "…Solomon answered all her questions; nothing was too difficult for him to explain." (2 Chronicles 9:2). She came with hard ones and he kept right on answering. Every question got an answer, so none of them stumped him.

Sleep, ha! I can see how a long inspection tour might feel that way. But the text says "…it took her breath away." (2 Chronicles 9:4). She saw the wisdom, the palace, the table, the servants and the offerings, and it left her breathless.

Other way around, friend. The queen says, "…not half of the greatness of your wisdom was told to me. You have far exceeded the report I heard." (2 Chronicles 9:6). She came ready to test him, and I think she left amazed. Nothing in her words says short.

Hiram's name does show up later in the passage, but not in her blessing. His servants are mentioned in 2 Chronicles 9:10. The queen says, "Blessed be the LORD your God…" (2 Chronicles 9:8). That's the name she lifts up after the servants.

Guards with harps would be a sight, friend, but that's not what the text says. The wood became "…lyres and harps for the singers." (2 Chronicles 9:11). Some of it also became steps for the house of the LORD and the king's palace. The instruments were made for the singers, not the guards.
